newsitem.title: USA: Oregon commission yet to review Enron offer.
newsitem.headline: Oregon commission yet to review Enron offer.

text.p: The staff of the Oregon Public Utility Commission (OPUC) will refrain from commenting on revised merger terms for Enron Corp and Portland General Corp until after they have had a chance to review details of the plan, a spokesman for the OPUC said Monday.
"We need to sit down and speak with Enron. Until such time as we see all the documents, we can't comment," said spokesman Mike Allegre.
He noted the companies appear to have met the staff's demand for an electricity rate cut of $141 million, but the exact terms and conditions of the offer are unknown.
The OPUC staff plans to meet with Enron officials today and on Tuesday to discuss the new terms, Allegre said.
On Friday, the staff recommended that the commission reject the $2.1 billion merger on the basis that Enron had not shown the merger would serve the interests of Portland General customers.
The companies announced today a revised merger agreement, including $141 million of merger-related benefits to customers.
Under the current schedule, the OPUC will make a final finding on the merger proposal in early June.
